label: INFINITE_1: Divine infinity is unboundedness of subsistent being not received in, and limited by…
term: infinite (ST I q.7; Lean parameter `Infinite` of `GodIsInfinite`)
definition: Divine infinity is unboundedness of subsistent being not received in, and limited by, anything (ST I q.7 a.1). It is the infinity of perfection, not an infinite quantity or indeterminate matter. Infinite is a primitive predicate supplied to GodIsInfinite and to ClassicalAttributesSuffice.
note: SubsistentBeingIsInfiniteReading gives only the sufficient condition esseOf x = essenceOf x → Infinite x, reading non-reception through q.3 a.4. Infinite has no definitional expansion imposing the full source account; the theorem remains conditional on that interpretation and premise.
